real_estate.homebuilder: Repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases; here, the typical first-time down payment on the five city median is about $90,000.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average stood at 7.50% at Friday's update, with the 15-year at 7.03%; Monday's reading had not posted by 8:15 AM PT. On today's $1,249,990 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $6,992 a month in principal and interest.

Repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases in the year to June, according to the National Association of REALTORS® 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers (chart). Their median age is 62 and first-time buyers' is 40, both tying records, and the typical buyer overall is now 58. The first-time share edged up to 22% from last year's record low of 21%.

Here, the gap is the down payment. NAR's median first-time buyer put down 9% and the median repeat buyer 19%. On our five city median list price of $999,988, that is about $90,000 down and $6,363 a month for the first-time buyer, against $190,000 down and $5,664 for the repeat buyer, at 7.50% before taxes and insurance. Equity from the last house is doing a lot of the lifting.

Monday's export shows 2,408 board wide, from 2,421 Sunday, with 134 coming soon and 144 brand new. The five city ledger is 606, from 616: Fremont (205) fell seven, Hayward (175) two and Newark (71) one, while Milpitas (98) and Union City (57) held.

What this means for you: first-time buyers, 9% down is the national norm, so get preapproved on what you have rather than waiting for 20%. Sellers, most of today's buyers arrive with equity, and a well priced home still draws them even at 7.50%.

• Board wide: 2,408 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 134 coming soon and 144 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 606 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 539 are on the market and 67 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 205 live, 164 active, 26 coming soon and 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,249,990 at $783 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 38 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 175, Milpitas 98, Newark 71, Union City 57.
• Across all five cities the median is $999,988 at $666 a square foot. 271 homes are priced under a million, and 188 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

feature_image.alt: Donut chart: repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases from July 2025 to June 2026 (median age 62, 19% median down payment) and first-time buyers 22% (median age 40, 9% down). Local panel: on the five city median list price of $999,988, 9% down is $90,000 and $6,363 a month in principal and interest at 7.50%; 19% down is $190,000 and $5,664 a month.
feature_image.caption: Repeat buyers dominate, and their bigger down payments cut the monthly cost by about $700 on our median home.
feature_image.source: National Association of REALTORS®, 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers; Mortgage News Daily; Bay East MLS export, Nov. 16, 2026

stocks.note: Levels are live at 8:15 AM PT Monday, November 16, against Friday's close. The market closes at 1:00 PM PT.
stocks.news:
Stocks slipped Monday morning, led by chips. At 8:15 AM PT the S&P 500 was down 1.22%, the Nasdaq 1.81% and the Dow 0.65%, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index was off 4.44%. Fremont's Lam Research was down 5.21% and Milpitas's KLA 4.20%.

Nvidia, down 2.57% at $158.66, reports quarterly results Tuesday after the close, its first since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. Market Briefs also expects Anthropic, the San Francisco company behind Claude, to go public this week; its filing offers 825 million shares at $70 to $78, up to about $64.4 billion. A busy week for Bay Area tickers.

economy.note: Live at 8:15 AM PT Monday: the 10-Year is CNBC's quote against Treasury's 5.15% Friday close, gold and silver are December COMEX futures against Friday's settlements, and Brent is Friday's ICE January settlement.
economy.commentary:
Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% from a year earlier, the fastest pace since November 2022 (chart). What builders pay for the materials in a new home rose 9.8%, also the fastest since November 2022, and that cost lands in the price of new construction. With consumer prices up 0.4% in October as well, a December rate increase stays on the table.

The 10-Year Treasury yield is near 5.13%, against Friday's 5.15% close. Gold is near $3,861.30, down 0.64% from Friday's settlement, and silver has dropped 5.11% to $46.61. Brent is down about 2.5% this morning near $93.49; the card shows Friday's $95.84 settlement.

feature_image.alt: Line chart, Producer Price Index change from a year earlier, not seasonally adjusted, October 2025 to October 2026: final demand rose from 2.8% to 6.5% and inputs to residential construction from 2.8% to 9.8%, both the fastest since November 2022.
feature_image.caption: Wholesale prices are up 6.5% from a year ago, and home building materials 9.8%.
feature_image.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Producer Price Index (October 2026 release; July to October preliminary)
